newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Ingush refugees die in Ossetia grenade attack.
newsitem.headline: Ingush refugees die in Ossetia grenade attack.

text.p: At least two refugees died and 10 were wounded in a grenade attack on a bus on Thursday in Russia's turbulent North Caucasus region, local authorities said.
The Ingush refugees were returning to the neighbouring North Ossetia region when their bus was fired on by grenade launchers, an Ingush presidential spokesman said.

"At least two were killed. Ten people were sent to hospital in a serious condition," Manlis Chakhkiyev, a spokesman for Ingushetia's President Ruslan Aushev, told Reuters by telephone. He said the bus carried 15 or 16 refugees.

It was not clear who carried out the attack, which took place only 15 km (10 miles) from the Ingush border. An armed conflict between North Ossetia and Ingushetia in 1992 killed about 200 and sparked a huge flow of Ingush refugees.

More than 20 attacks against Ingush refugees returning to their homes in the Prigorodny district, which is controlled by North Ossetia, have been committed in the last month, raising ethnic tension in the turbulent North Caucasus.
The Ingush side pinned the blame for the attacks on North Ossetians.
Aushev told Interfax on Thursday he saw the attacks as a concerted attempt to destabilise the situation and urged Russian President Boris Yeltsin to introduce direct presidential rule.
Earlier this week Aushev sent a cable to Yeltsin warning him that tensions with the neighbouring region had increased sharply and appealing for him to impose direct presidential rule in the region.

The seeds of the conflict lie in Soviet dictator Josef Stalin's deportation of the entire Ingush people to Central Asia during World War Two. Much of their land was taken over by Ossetians, but in the early 1990s Ingushis tried to return. Fighting erupted, causing a serious refugee problem in tiny Ingushetia.
